security_audit.summary: The skill documents local TCP printing and a localhost management interface. Most static findings are Markdown examples or local-network addresses, but the documented export to launchd and Windows Task Scheduler creates persistent system tasks and requires user review.

remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit confirmation immediately before exporting or registering a launchd or Windows scheduled task. Show the generated command or plist and provide a removal command.
Document that scheduled tasks should invoke only a fixed local script with validated printer configuration and should not accept arbitrary command text.
Ask for confirmation before installing Python dependencies and pin or document the dependency versions.

remediation.issue: Missing implementation files in the published tree
remediation.suggestion: Include the referenced scripts or revise the documentation so users can verify the commands and network behavior before use.

content.value_statement: Restaurant teams need a repeatable way to send task sheets and checklists to thermal printers. This skill helps configure local printers, test connectivity, and format print jobs.
actual_capabilities: Guides configuration of named local-network Meituan printers using an IP address and port.
Tests printer reachability with the documented local connectivity command.
Formats task sheets, checklists, and receipts for ESC/POS thermal printers.
Routes a print request by configured alias or a directly provided IP address.
Explains a localhost web interface for printer, template, and schedule management.
Documents daily, weekly, and monthly printing schedules.
limitations: The referenced Python scripts are not included in the audited file tree.
It requires a compatible Meituan thermal printer on the same local network.
It does not verify successful paper output after a network send.
System-level scheduling can create persistent tasks and needs explicit user review.

use_cases.title: Print kitchen task sheets
use_cases.description: Send a formatted shift checklist to a named kitchen printer.

use_cases.title: Set up a front-desk printer
use_cases.description: Add a printer alias, validate its local address, and test connectivity.

use_cases.title: Plan recurring checklists
use_cases.description: Prepare a daily, weekly, or monthly print schedule for routine operations.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: print a task sheet
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me send a one-time task sheet to the kitchen printer. Ask for the title and content first.

prompt_templates.title: Configure a printer
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a printer named Front Desk. Ask for its local IP address, port, and purpose, then test connectivity.

prompt_templates.title: Create a formatted checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a thermal-printer checklist for the evening shift with time sections and clear task lines.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: review a schedule
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a weekday printing schedule for the stock checklist. Show the proposed command or task definition and ask before creating any persistent system task.

output_examples.input: Print an opening checklist for the kitchen at 09:30.
output: Content includes a 09:30 section and the requested tasks
Status: Ready to send after confirmation

output_examples.input: Add a printer called Front Desk at a local address.
output: Next step: Run the documented connectivity check
Configuration changes require confirmation before saving

best_practices: Confirm the printer alias, content, and whether the request is one-time or scheduled before sending.
Use private local-network addresses and verify the printer is on the same network.
Review generated launchd or Task Scheduler definitions before creating persistent tasks.
anti_patterns: Do not print to an unrecognized IP address without confirming ownership and purpose.
Do not create a persistent scheduled task without showing its command and obtaining approval.
Do not assume a successful connection test proves that paper printed correctly.

faq.question: What printers does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets compatible Meituan thermal printers that accept local TCP and ESC/POS print jobs.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: The documented printing flow uses the local network. The web interface uses localhost.

faq.question: Can I use printer names instead of addresses?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents aliases such as Kitchen or Front Desk after configuration.

faq.question: What is the default printer port?
faq.answer: The documentation uses port 9100 as the default for compatible printers.

faq.question: Can it schedule recurring printing?
faq.answer: It documents daily, weekly, and monthly schedules. Persistent system tasks require explicit review.

faq.question: Are the printing scripts included?
faq.answer: No. The audited file tree does not include the referenced scripts, so verify their source before running them.
